text:
Alex: quick heads-up — our streaming integration tests started throwing 401s after we switched the CI runner to windows-latest. Non-stream endpoints are fine. anyone seen this? suspecting API_KEY env or header formatting.

Ben: have you checked for trailing CRLF or BOM on the secret? windows runners (and some editors) can sneak in \r. try trimming. also check how you build the Basic header — a stray \r will break the base64 payload.

Carla: quick cheatsheet: basic auth for our API uses `Authorization: Basic <base64(\"apikey:<KEY>\")>` — if <KEY> has a newline the header decodes incorrectly. examples: 

bash (unix):
`echo -n \"apikey:$REDWOOD_API_KEY\" | base64`

PowerShell (avoid Get-Content raw newline):
```
$raw = Get-Content secret.txt -Raw
$key = $raw -replace "`r|`n", ""
[Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetBytes("apikey:$key"))
```

Ben: also for GH Actions on windows, secrets injected via files or actions steps can include a trailing newline. quick safe fixes: `.trim()` or a `tr -d '\r\n'` when reading the file.

Emma: adding Node-specific note — if you do `fs.readFileSync('/run/secrets/REDWOOD_API_KEY', 'utf8')` you'll often get a trailing \n. minimal safe snippet: 
```
const key = require('fs').readFileSync('/run/secrets/REDWOOD_API_KEY', 'utf8').trim();
const auth = 'Basic ' + Buffer.from(`apikey:${key}`).toString('base64');
// fetch with { headers: { Authorization: auth } }
```

Alex: we actually build header in the test harness (js) and pass it to a curl subprocess for streaming. probably the string has a \r. repro I ran: 
```
# problematic (adds newline on some systems)
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Basic $(echo \"apikey:$(cat key.txt)\" | base64)\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream
# safe
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Basic $(echo -n \"apikey:$(cat key.txt | tr -d '\\r')\" | base64)\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream
```

Carla: another gotcha: Windows `setx` persists without trimming; `set` vs `setx` behavior differs. For ephemeral runner env use `$env:REDWOOD_API_KEY = (Get-Content secret.txt -Raw).Trim()` in pwsh step.

Ben: also check BOM (UTF-8 BOM) — base64 of `\xef\xbb\xbfapikey:KEY` will totally differ. remove BOM with `sed '1s/^\xEF\xBB\xBF//'` or use encoding-aware readers.

ci-bot: [automated] added `ci` label to thread.

Alex: awesome, thanks. I'll trim + remove BOM and re-run. pinging here once the CI green. :thumbsup:
